messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: blending Stan with interfaces
parts:
Hi!

Following on the discussion on "testify" which resulted in a planned delayed generated quantitiy block as far as I understood. Here is why I think you could reconsider this more in a direction of "testify":

Quite a number of scientific software is written as a mix of languages, i.e. a very successfull model is to code most of data handling/fiddling/processing/whatever thing in something "light" like R or Python. Then the hard stuff should always be done in something like C++. At least this is how I have done much of my research. Following this approach means that Stan should opt to make possibly all those tremendous functionality in Stan not only available in those few blocks, but rather it should be the goal to bridge Stan space with the interface space.

This is a bit contrary to the current approach "keep the interfaces lean and let the C++ Stan handle" - but only in some sense. What would be awesome to have at some point is to tie all those Stan function into the interfaces you have, i.e. I would find it extremely helpful to just straight be abel to call lkj densities from R. Of course, not all interfaces are as rich as others, but then languages like R are so powerful that not making use of this would be a pitty. Just an example, with the current testify stuff I can define a Stan functions, which, say, takes the two parameters a and b as argument. Then having the function in R space allows me to do stuff like

testify("model.stan") which has "real calc_stuff(real a, real b) {}"

# also assume we have a fit

post <- extract(fit, c("a", "b"))

do.call(Vectorize(calc_stuff), post)

Now, the last call is likely awkward looking for anyone not programming R for a while, but it is a nice example of how easy some things are in R, i.e. I get almost for free a mechanism to do posterior simulations in a very straightforward way.

And one more argument for blending Stan into the interfaces - each of us is best in commanding with the interfaces the objects we care about. Hence, fitting Stan tightly into the user environment is a huge step.

I am speaking here as a user, of course. Software wise, I think there are approaches as Swig which goes beyond R (for R we have the wonderful Rcpp) which may we worth to consider.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] blending Stan with interfaces
parts:
I agree.  Especially cos it’s a real pain in the ass to write Fortran or C programs and run from R.  Being able to run Stan programs from R is a real plus.  Which, now, with testify, we have.
A
